links.comparator_used: Head-to-head comparison of four UQ methods (probability entropy, Monte Carlo dropout, deep ensembles, test time augmentation) on the same 3D U-Net; no point-prediction-only arm
links.outcome: Uncertainty measure performance for degraded image detection, false-positive detection, false-negative recovery, and correlation with biomarker capture and segmentation metrics
links.effect: Degraded image detection AUC, test time augmentation vs probability entropy: low 0.68 vs 0.54, medium 0.82 vs 0.70, high 0.90 vs 0.83. FP detection AUC 0.77-0.81 for all methods. Correlations: TTA best for SUVtotal (rho=0.57) and Dice (rho=0.72), MC dropout best for SUVmean (rho=0.35), probability entropy best for cross entropy (rho=0.96).
links.quote: Overall, test time augmentation demonstrated superior UQ performance and is recommended for use in metastatic lesion segmentation task.
